inline_comments.comment: The `key="icon"` prop on these SVG elements is a no-op. React `key` is only meaningful for elements rendered inside an iterable (e.g., a `.map()` call or an array) to help reconciliation. These JSX nodes are stored as static values in `StatusIconMap` and then rendered directly as `{changeIcon}` — not inside a list — so React silently discards the key. Remove `key="icon"` from all three new SVG entries.

`textColor` is now derived exclusively from `testStatus`, silently dropping the original behavior where it was computed from the most-critical status across all statuses. A story with only a change-detection status (e.g., `status-value:new`) will have `testStatus = 'status-value:unknown'`; `getStatus` for `unknown` returns no `textColor`, so the story label text will lose its color tint entirely. If the intent is to reserve text coloring for test statuses only, document that decision with a comment. Otherwise, derive `textColor` from the combined most-critical status — e.g., `getMostCriticalStatusValue([changeStatus, testStatus])` — so change-detection statuses continue to affect label color.

`getChangeDetectionStatus` is a pure data-transformation function with no UI dependencies, yet it is exported from `Tree.tsx` (a UI component) instead of `status.ts`, where the closely related `getMostCriticalStatusValue`, `getGroupStatus`, and other status helpers live. This conflates concerns and forces the unit test to import a utility function through the component's full module graph. Moving it to `status.ts` would make it easier to discover, test in isolation, and reuse.

`statusOrder` does not appear to be used anywhere in this file — `getMostCriticalStatusValue` (imported from `status.ts`) uses its own internal `statusPriority` array for priority determination. If `statusOrder` truly has no consumers, updating it is misleading and the array should be removed. If it is used elsewhere (e.g., for display ordering), the new placement of `'status-value:error'` after `'status-value:warning'` in the array is a behavior change from the pre-PR ordering and should be explicitly justified.

The test-status button uses `ariaLabel={\`Status: ${testStatus.replace('status-value:', '')}\`}` while the adjacent change-detection button uses `"Change status: X"`. Now that two status buttons coexist in the same leaf node, `"Status: X"` is ambiguous for screen-reader users who will hear both announcements in sequence. Use `"Test status: X"` to be symmetrical with the sibling button and unambiguous.

The `'priority within change-detection slot'` test populates `StatusByTypeId` with three entries sharing `typeId: 'storybook/change-detection'` under the keys `first`, `second`, and `third`, requiring `as unknown as StatusByTypeId` to bypass the type. Since `StatusByTypeId = Record<StatusTypeId, Status>`, there can be at most one entry per `typeId` key at runtime, making this scenario unreachable in production. Consider replacing this test with a realistic case, or — if multiple distinct change-detection providers with different typeIds are an intended future use — model the test that way and remove the cast.

This test calls `getMostCriticalStatusValue` (from `status.ts`), not `getChangeDetectionStatus`, so it does not belong in the `dual-slot status splitting` describe block. Move it to the existing `getHighestStatus` suite to keep each suite focused on a single function and to make failures clearly attributable.

general_comments.comment: None of the five new story variants (`WithChangeDetectionOnly`, `WithChangeDetectionAndTestStatus`, `WithTestStatusOnly`, `WithAffectedStatus`, `BranchWithChangeDetectionPriority`) include a `play` function. The central behavioral claim of this PR — that two independent status icon slots render correctly for various status combinations — is validated only visually. Each story should use `canvas.getByTestId('tree-change-status-button')` / `getByTestId('tree-status-button')` assertions (or `getByRole('button', { name: ... })`) to confirm the correct buttons appear and disappear per the given `allStatuses` input, catching regressions automatically.
